punchline: People who always hunt for the best option report being less happy than people who stop at good enough.
thirty_sec: Barry Schwartz splits people into two kinds of choosers. Maximizers need the best option, so they keep checking. Satisficers have their own standards and stop once something meets them. In questionnaire research by Schwartz and colleagues, maximizers reported less happiness, less optimism and more regret. His advice: choose when to choose. Settle for good enough on most things, and save the full search for decisions that really matter.
question: What's one area of your life where you always want the best, and one where good enough works just fine?
